clue.text: Prince warned about …

indicators.note: about can mean round and around, all over the place, so the letters of warned are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A royal who cautioned someone, with the sentence trailing off into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this clue to 4 Across, whose surface continues the sentence; for solving, each clue stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duke of York is a British royal holding that title, the second son of Elizabeth II.

clue.text: TV presenter upset sister of 1 Across, one feels

parts.note: Ant McPartlin is half of the British TV presenting duo Ant and Dec

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Princess Anne is the sister of the prince at 1 Across

explanation.surface: A television host has distressed the prince's sister, someone senses.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a well-known British presenting pair. 'upset' turns ANNE into ENNA.
explanation.definitionFit: An insect's feeler is the sensory organ it uses to touch and sense, so it is something that feels.

clue.text: One calling Liverpool fan up about score draw?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the draw
up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Liverpool FC are known as the Reds, so a supporter is a red
a score draw is a tied match with goals, such as one-all, written with I for one

explanation.surface: A football supporter phoning a pools line about a drawn match.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football pools a score draw is a tie with goals. 'up' turns RED into DER, which goes 'about' I ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person making a telephone call is one who dials, so a caller.

clue.text: Revealing postal orders kept by former Dutch bank

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so the orders sit within the other letters

parts.note: ex means former
ING is a large Dutch banking group
PO is the abbreviation for a postal order, so POS for the plural

explanation.surface: A scandal: money orders hidden at a now-defunct Dutch bank are brought to light.
explanation.definitionFit: Laying something bare or uncovering it is a synonym for revealing.

clue.text: … body part possibly dripping, I hear — not a problem

indicators.note: the speaker says the phrase is caught by ear, so what is spoken is swapped for a similar-sounding phrase

parts.note: a nose is one example of a body part, and dripping means wet, giving nose wet

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 Across: the prince cautioned about some sweaty part of the body, then shrugged it off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is casual reassurance that a task is easy and causes no bother at all.

clue.text: Pinch a little bit of booze

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to squeeze sharply between the fingers
a small measure of spirits, a dram or tot

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a squeeze between finger and thumb and a small drink of spirits.

clue.text: Scattered boxes on base

parts.note: a boxer who practises against a partner spars
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A boxer in training is fighting on a military base, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a down clue puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinly spread and few in number is what scattered means here.

clue.text: Sculptor putting extreme pressure on mug

parts.note: EP is the technical abbreviation for extreme pressure, used of lubricants
a stein is a large beer mug

explanation.surface: An artist forcing his clay hard onto a drinking vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... on' sets the first piece above the second in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was an American-born British sculptor, a pioneer of modern sculpture.

clue.text: He wrote play after opening retracted

indicators.note: after puts the word for play following the other piece
retracted means drawn back, so the word for opening is read backwards

parts.note: a slot is a narrow opening
to toy with something is to play with it

explanation.surface: An author who wrote a drama after its first night was cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' and 'opening' look theatrical but give TOY and SLOT; 'retracted' turns SLOT into TOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy, author of War and Peace, is a famous writer, so he wrote.

clue.text: Carol's part in training pandas perhaps

indicators.note: in training suggests the letters are being drilled and reshaped into a new form

explanation.surface: A singer called Carol plays a role in getting pandas to breed or perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pandas' looks like the animals, but panda cars were British police patrol vehicles, once painted in blue and white panels.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain police vehicles were nicknamed panda cars, so pandas are examples of these.

clue.text: Vagrant male in role reversal

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for male inside the other piece
reversal tells us the synonym for role is read from end to start

parts.note: an actor's role is a part

explanation.surface: A man taking on the part of a homeless drifter, the reverse of his usual roles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversal' turns PART into TRAP, and M goes in to give TRA-M-P.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant is a homeless wanderer, which is the noun sense of a tramp or vagabond.

clue.text: Dismay about Italian TV station's evaluation

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for dismay goes round the broadcaster

parts.note: to dismay someone is to appal them
RAI is Italy's state broadcaster; the possessive supplies the S

explanation.surface: Someone is dismayed by a critical review from an Italian television channel.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment of worth or quality is a synonym for an evaluation.

clue.text: Penniless, essentially, having nothing

indicators.note: essentially points at the essence or core of the word, so its central letters are taken

explanation.surface: Being broke basically means having no money at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes the middle three letters of PENNILESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A word for zero, used especially for sports scores, is a synonym for nothing.

clue.text: Emphasise these changes in engineer's drawing

parts.note: to emphasise something is to stress it

indicators.note: changes asks for the letters of these to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to underline these alterations on a technical plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges THESE into SHEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers draw up a document of this kind showing the forces and loads on a structure's parts.

clue.text: Brass or strings, for example, synthesised on cheesy CD

indicators.note: synthesised means put together artificially, so the letters are recombined in a new order

explanation.surface: Orchestral sections faked electronically on a tacky compact disc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brass or strings' look like music, but each names a group of players by their instrument, a part standing for the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A figure of speech in which a part names the whole; brass naming the players is an example.

clue.text: Hormone replacement initially covered in a study leading to some dishonest statement

indicators.note: leading to puts the first part in front of what follows
covered in says the initial letter is enclosed inside the word for a study

parts.note: a den is a private room or study

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word replacement

parts.note: some can stand for the indefinite article a
to spin someone a line is to tell them something untrue

explanation.surface: Hormone replacement therapy research ends up as a misleading claim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hormone replacement' looks like one phrase but splits: 'Hormone' is the definition. 'covered in' puts R inside the study; 'some' supplies the article A, and spinning someone a line means lying.
explanation.definitionFit: A hormone released by the adrenal glands in response to stress or excitement.

clue.text: A duke seen in New York?

definitions.text: A duke seen in New York?

indicators.note: seen in puts the abbreviation for duke inside the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which nobleman might turn up in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: Prince Andrew, nicknamed this, is the Duke of York, so he is a duke found in New York with an extra word added.
explanation.definitionFit: This nickname belongs to Prince Andrew, who held the title Duke of York, matching the prince at 1 Across.

clue.text: Act as a preliminary for a unionist party statement finally being accepted by Varadkar

indicators.note: being accepted by means taken in, so the pieces go inside the forename

parts.note: Leo Varadkar is a former Irish Taoiseach
the DUP is Northern Ireland's Democratic Unionist Party

indicators.note: finally takes the final letter of the word statement

explanation.surface: An Irish politics story: a unionist party's statement is finally accepted by the Taoiseach.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo Varadkar served as Ireland's prime minister; the Democratic Unionist Party is a Northern Irish party.
explanation.definitionFit: To precede and prepare the way for something is to act as a preliminary to it.

clue.text: Seedy guy regularly getting nervous

indicators.note: regularly takes letters at a steady interval, here the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: A shady-looking man becoming jittery.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tense, on edge and jumpy is a synonym for nervous.

clue.text: Go after key article for one who's got away

indicators.note: after places the word for go following the other pieces

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
a is the indefinite article
to go, in the informal toilet sense, is to pee

explanation.surface: An instruction to chase a crucial item belonging to a fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' looks like 'pursue', but it is the informal word for urinating.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has fled from captivity or prison is someone who has got away.

clue.text: At first girl simply removed item of clothing

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word girl
removed means moved away from its original form, so the letters of simply are rearranged

explanation.surface: A girl just took off a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed' rearranges SIMPLY into YMSLIP. A gymslip is a sleeveless tunic once worn by British schoolgirls.
explanation.definitionFit: A sleeveless pinafore tunic once standard in girls' school uniforms is a garment.

clue.text: Severe criticism of chopper's role

parts.note: a hatchet is a small axe, a chopper
a job is a role or function

explanation.surface: A question of what work an axe does.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a hatchet's function; the phrase it builds is the idiom for a savage attack in print.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a fierce, often malicious written attack on a person or their work.

clue.text: Bath copper getting into music that's on Island

indicators.note: getting into puts the symbol inside the word for music

parts.note: jazz is a genre of music
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A policeman takes a bath while music plays on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool tub with underwater jets is a kind of bath, named after its inventors.

clue.text: Cosmic event covered in large report

parts.note: large means big
a report is a loud noise such as a gunshot or a bang

explanation.surface: A cosmic happening is described in a lengthy document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report' looks like a document but is the noise of an explosion.
explanation.definitionFit: The theory of the universe's origin names the explosion that began it, an event on a cosmic scale.

clue.text: Weakness of one former car manufacturer assimilated by rival

indicators.note: assimilated by means absorbed into, so the pieces go inside the word for rival

parts.note: a foe is an opponent or rival
I is the Roman numeral for one
BL is British Leyland, a defunct British car maker

explanation.surface: A business story: a defunct carmaker's flaw is swallowed up by its competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: British Leyland was a large British car company of the 1970s and 80s.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor flaw or quirk of character is a small weakness.

clue.text: Complaint about Maitlis at last: "A troublesome woman"

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the illness goes round the letter

parts.note: a complaint is an illness; the everyday virus giving a runny nose fits

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the name Maitlis

explanation.surface: A grumble about the broadcaster Emily Maitlis, labelling her a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Emily Maitlis is a British TV news presenter. 'Complaint' wants to be the definition; it is the illness wrapped round S.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a quarrelsome, nagging woman who disturbed the peace could be charged in English law under this name.

clue.text: One playing a small part in Scrooge regularly

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth of the miser's name

explanation.surface: An actor with a bit part in a production of A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor, replaceable person in a large organisation is called this, by analogy with a tooth on a gearwheel.

clue.text: Live in Clapham, perhaps — a major resort and tourist centre

definitions.text: a major resort and tourist centre

indicators.note: in places the verb for live inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests the letters of the place name might be arranged another way

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: Residing in a south London district, then a remark about a big holiday destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Clapham is a district of south London; 'perhaps' shuffles its letters, and 'in' places the verb for live within them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy town on Florida's Atlantic coast, famous as a winter holiday destination.

clue.text: Pompous fool one found on ship

parts.note: a means one
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A self-important idiot is discovered on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupid, foolish person, often a self-important one, is called a donkey in insult.

clue.text: Some paparazzi phoned back to get something to eat

indicators.note: back means the extracted letters are read from right to left
some says only part of the text is used, letters taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: Press photographers called again to order a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks AZZIP out of 'paparazzi phoned' and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian baked dish of dough with toppings is an example of food.

clue.text: Fast, say

definitions.meaning: an adjective for a train or delivery service that is quick, making few stops
a verb meaning to put into words, to state or convey

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both rapid, as of a train, and to put into words.

clue.text: Surrey town without a royal personage

parts.note: W/O is a common written abbreviation for without
a king is a royal personage

explanation.surface: A commuter town that lacks any royalty.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is an English county just south-west of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A large commuter town in the county of Surrey, south-west of London.
